examples.title: 5. Singers in 2014 concerts: the correct head (multi-join), set by hand

result.question: What are the names of the singers who performed in a concert in 2014?
result.label: multi-join

base.sql: SELECT T3.Name FROM concert AS T1 JOIN singer_in_concert AS T2 ON T1.concert_ID = T2.concert_ID JOIN singer AS T3 ON T2.Singer_ID = T3.Singer_ID WHERE T1.Year = '2014'

lora.sql: SELECT T3.Name FROM singer_in_concert AS T1 JOIN concert AS T2 ON T1.concert_ID  =  T2.concert_ID JOIN singer AS T3 ON T1.Singer_ID  =  T3.Singer_ID WHERE T2.Year  =  2014

hydra.sql: SELECT T3.Name FROM singer_in_concert AS T1 JOIN concert AS T2 ON T1.concert_ID  =  T2.concert_ID JOIN singer AS T3 ON T1.Singer_ID  =  T3.Singer_ID WHERE T2.Year  =  2014
hydra.head: multi-join

examples.title: 8. Aggregation with a join: cities per continent

result.question: How many cities are there in each continent?
result.label: aggregation
result.label_note: Live classifier says: **aggregation** (it is right only about 59% of the time)

base.sql: SELECT Continent, COUNT(*) FROM city GROUP BY Continent

lora.sql: SELECT count(*) ,  T1.Continent FROM country AS T1 JOIN city AS T2 ON T1.Code  =  T2.CountryCode GROUP BY T1.Continent

hydra.sql: SELECT Continent ,  count(*) FROM city GROUP BY Continent
hydra.head: aggregation
